headline.title: Announcing our partnership with the Republic of Korea
headline.summary: Google DeepMind has announced a partnership with the Republic of Korea to enhance scientific research through the application of advanced AI models. This collaboration aims to accelerate breakthroughs in various scientific fields by leveraging frontier AI technologies.

articles.title: Feedback Over Form: Why Execution Feedback Matters More Than Pipeline Topology in 1-3B Code Generation
articles.summary: A study published on arXiv investigates the effectiveness of execution feedback in enhancing the performance of small language models (1-3B) for code generation tasks. The research finds that incorporating execution feedback into code generation pipelines is more beneficial than simply increasing the complexity of the pipeline structure.

articles.title: Verbal Confidence Saturation in 3-9B Open-Weight Instruction-Tuned LLMs: A Pre-Registered Psychometric Validity Screen
articles.summary: A study assessed the verbal confidence outputs of seven instruction-tuned open-weight language models with 3-9 billion parameters to determine their validity for uncertainty estimation. The research involved administering 524 TriviaQA items and aimed to evaluate the models' ability to meet criteria for Type-2 discrimination in verbal confidence elicitation.

articles.title: Controllable Spoken Dialogue Generation: An LLM-Driven Grading System for K-12 Non-Native English Learners
articles.summary: A new framework for controllable spoken dialogue generation has been developed to better serve K-12 non-native English learners by aligning large language model outputs with their proficiency levels. This system utilizes a four-tier grading approach based on China's national curriculum to adjust lexical complexity according to learner abilities.

articles.title: UR$^2$: Unify RAG and Reasoning through Reinforcement Learning
articles.summary: The article presents UR$^2$, a framework that aims to unify Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) to enhance the capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) in knowledge grounding and complex reasoning. It addresses the limitations of previous approaches by expanding beyond fixed retrieval settings, allowing for better generalization across various domains.

articles.title: OmniOVCD: Streamlining Open-Vocabulary Change Detection with SAM 3
articles.summary: The article presents OmniOVCD, a new approach to Open-Vocabulary Change Detection (OVCD) that simplifies the process by integrating the Segment Anything Model (SAM) without the need for additional models like DINO. This method aims to enhance the detection of land cover changes over time while minimizing reliance on predefined categories.

articles.title: DVGT-2: Vision-Geometry-Action Model for Autonomous Driving at Scale
articles.summary: The paper introduces the Vision-Geometry-Action (VGA) model for autonomous driving, emphasizing the importance of dense 3D geometry as a key component for navigation and planning. This approach contrasts with existing vision-language-action models by prioritizing geometric cues to enhance end-to-end driving capabilities.

articles.title: Lifting Unlabeled Internet-level Data for 3D Scene Understanding
articles.summary: Researchers propose a method to utilize unlabeled internet videos for generating training data to improve 3D scene understanding models. The study highlights the effectiveness of data engines in overcoming challenges associated with automated data generation, complementing existing human-annotated datasets.

articles.title: LLM+Graph@VLDB'2025 Workshop Summary
articles.summary: The 2nd LLM+Graph Workshop, held alongside VLDB 2025 in London, explored the integration of large language models with graph-structured data, highlighting advancements in algorithms and systems for this emerging research area. The workshop attracted significant interest from both academia and industry, emphasizing the importance of bridging LLMs with graph data management and machine learning.

articles.title: Math Takes Two: A test for emergent mathematical reasoning in communication
articles.summary: Researchers propose "Math Takes Two," a new test designed to evaluate emergent mathematical reasoning in language models, distinguishing between true reasoning and mere statistical pattern matching. The test aims to assess models' abilities to construct abstract concepts from first principles, addressing limitations in current evaluations that focus on established mathematical conventions.

articles.title: An Artifact-based Agent Framework for Adaptive and Reproducible Medical Image Processing
articles.summary: The article presents an artifact-based agent framework designed to enhance adaptability and reproducibility in medical image processing. It emphasizes the need for dataset-aware workflow configuration and provenance tracking to facilitate the transition from benchmark evaluation to real-world clinical applications.

articles.title: MolClaw: An Autonomous Agent with Hierarchical Skills for Drug Molecule Evaluation, Screening, and Optimization
articles.summary: MolClaw is an autonomous agent designed to enhance drug molecule evaluation, screening, and optimization by integrating over 30 specialized tools into a cohesive workflow. This approach addresses the challenges faced by current AI agents in maintaining performance during complex drug discovery processes.
